runs.label: CRM / FTD anomaly
runs.question: Why did European FTD conversion deteriorate after July 15?
findings: Affected Europe Team A+B FTD conversion changed by -7.53 percentage points after 2026-07-15.
Median response time in the affected cohort changed by 29.15 minutes.
The European control cohort conversion changed by -1.21 percentage points over the same split.
A CRM routing change is present in the nearby business-event log and is a supported root-cause candidate, not an automatically proven real-world causal conclusion.
Team A is the largest negative team-level contributor in the symmetric Europe FTD-rate decomposition (-1.87 pp contribution).
8 of 27 post-change daily response-time medians exceed the robust pre-change high-anomaly threshold.
runs.guardrail: The evidence supports the CRM routing change as the primary root-cause candidate in this synthetic benchmark; a real deployment should not convert temporal association into a causal claim without additional design/validation.

runs.label: Net-deposit anomaly
runs.question: Why did European net deposits fall in the week starting August 3?
findings: European net deposits changed by $-187,790.90 week over week (2026-07-27–2026-08-02 versus 2026-08-03–2026-08-09).
Deposits changed by $59,158.18, while withdrawals changed by $246,949.08; the decomposition exactly reconstructs the net-deposit movement.
The largest 11 European customer withdrawals account for 91.6% of current-week European withdrawals.
Europe's weekly net-deposit movement per registered customer was $-27.74, versus a median of $9.43 across the other regions.

A high-value withdrawal-cluster event is present in the nearby operational event log. Together with the measured withdrawal concentration, this is a supported observed driver, not evidence of why individual customers withdrew.
runs.guardrail: The evidence supports concentrated high-value withdrawals as an observed driver of the synthetic net-deposit deterioration. It does not establish why those customers withdrew or justify an investment, compliance, or customer-risk conclusion without additional evidence.

runs.label: Customer Intelligence
runs.question: How are European customer segments distributed by behavioral value, and which segment contributes most to deposits?
findings: FitzSight segmented 6,770 European customers into 4 transparent behavioral-value groups with 100% coverage.
High Value is the largest deposit-value segment, accounting for 53.7% of completed European deposits in the synthetic dataset.
High Value customers average $10,622.51 in completed deposits, versus $0.00 for Low Activity customers.
High Value accounts for the largest segment share of completed withdrawals (63.7%); this is descriptive withdrawal pressure, not evidence of customer motive or suspicious behavior.
The segmentation is a descriptive operational analytics layer and must not be used as an automated credit, AML, suitability, eligibility or adverse-action decision.
runs.guardrail: Behavioral segments are descriptive analytical groupings only. They are not credit, AML, suitability, eligibility, or adverse-action decisions.

runs.label: Marketing lead quality
runs.question: Why did Americas lead volume rise while FTD conversion fell after June 15?
findings: Americas lead volume increased by 838 leads (+315.0%) in the equal post-campaign window.
Americas FTD conversion changed by -10.84 percentage points, with a two-proportion p-value of 2.466e-06.
Paid Search share of Americas leads changed by +60.52 percentage points; Paid Search conversion changed by -16.44 percentage points and had the largest negative within-channel performance effect.
A paid-media expansion appears in the nearby synthetic operations log and aligns with the measured volume/mix shift; it is treated as a supported candidate context, not a universal causal rule.
runs.guardrail: The synthetic evidence supports a Paid Search acquisition-quality shift as the primary observed driver: lead volume and Paid Search mix rose while conversion deteriorated and Paid Search had the largest negative within-channel performance effect. This benchmark does not justify claims about customer motives or prove that paid media is intrinsically low quality.

runs.label: False-correlation guardrail
runs.question: Why did Asia FTD conversion fall after July 20, and is the nearby office relocation the cause?
findings: Asia FTD conversion changed by -8.13 percentage points across the July 20 split.
Affiliate has the largest negative within-channel performance effect; its conversion rate changed by -15.81 percentage points.
The Affiliate-specific conversion shift has p=0.004634 under the two-proportion test.
An office-relocation event appears nearby in time, but its declared scope/effect does not support a lead-conversion explanation; FitzSight therefore rejects that event as the cause in this benchmark.
runs.guardrail: Temporal proximity is not treated as causality. The synthetic data support an Affiliate-specific conversion deterioration as the observed driver, while the nearby office-relocation event is explicitly not supported as the cause. FitzSight does not infer why Affiliate quality changed without additional evidence.
